title: Microstream ergonomics and structured tools proposal
content:
Summary:
This is a working sketch for a small-footprint streaming mode ("microstream") that prioritizes ultra-low-latency token-by-token handoff for mobile and embedded SDKs while preserving support for structured tool calls and typed outputs. Goal is an SDK-friendly surface with a minimal wire contract so 3rd-party clients can implement fast, incremental UIs without needing the full streaming protocol complexity we use for web/desktop clients.

Why this exists (motivation):
- Mobile UIs in customer pilots report 150–300ms perceived typing lag when we use our current chunking defaults.
- Some partners want deterministic tool-call boundaries and small frames for bandwidth-constrained networks (satcom, poor cellular).
- Embedded customers (on-device webviews) want a simple callback model they can adopt quickly: tiny payloads, few stateful frames, and straightforward error semantics.

Primary goals:
- Sub-100ms first-token-to-UI display in common 4G mobile scenarios (measured p50).
- Deterministic tool-call semantics: clear begin/commit/abort signals that an SDK can map to local transactions.
- Keep the network contract tiny: deliver single-token / small-chunk frames that are self-descriptive and replay-safe.
- Provide an opt-in typed-structure channel for adapters to declare JSON schemas for final outputs (useful for action synthesis).
- Minimal implementation overhead for client SDKs: 3 callbacks (onPartialText, onToolFrame, onCommit) + 1 tiny handshake.

Key scenarios to support:
1) Mobile compose box: user types prompt, model streams reply characters/words; UI shows partial text live and can display a "tool suggestion card" when the model emits a tool frame.
2) Embedded assistant with payment tool: model emits a tool call to a payment adapter; SDK must show a confirm banner and only call the tool after user confirmation.
3) Low-bandwidth fallback: client switches to microstream in poor networks, receives smaller frames and gets a final structured output schema that is easier to validate locally.
4) Resumability: client may reconnect after a short dropout and request replay from a token offset; frames must allow deterministic replay without complex session state.

Wire contract (sketch):
- Client handshake: POST /v1/microstream with body {"model":"x", "mode":"microstream", "schema": optional JSON schema URL, "resume_token": optional}
- Server responses: newline-delimited JSON minimal frames: each line is a single JSON object. Frames are intentionally tiny. Types: 
  - {"t":"tok","seq":int,"text":"..."}  (small pieces of text, token or word-level depending on model config)
  - {"t":"tool_start","id":"uuid","tool":"payment/qa/search","meta":{...}}  (signals a tool invocation start)
  - {"t":"tool_arg","id":"uuid","arg":"{...}"} (one or more small arg frames; for big args, use URL reference)
  - {"t":"tool_commit","id":"uuid","outcome":"pending|confirmed|aborted"}  (explicit commit/abort semantics)
  - {"t":"final","checksum":"sha256","schema_verified":bool,"structured_url":optional}  (end frame with optional pointer to structured payload)
- Replay/resume: allow client to request resume_token=seq_last_received+1. Server must be able to stream from that token or return an error if not available.

Tool calling rules (client-facing):
- Tools must be surfaced to the client as first-class "tool frames". SDK should raise a UI affordance immediately on tool_start.
- The default behavior is NOT to auto-execute tools. Clients must explicitly confirm via an SDK method (e.g., client.confirmTool(id)). This avoids surprise side-effects.
- For partners who opt-in to server-executed tools, use an explicit flag in the handshake: "tool_execution":"server|client|disabled". If "server", tool_start implies server will run tool and send tool_commit/outcome afterward.

Structured output / typed channel:
- If client provides a schema URL in handshake, the server will attempt to emit a structured payload and will set schema_verified when the final object matches the schema.
- Structured payloads may be large; the microstream contract allows a final pointer (structured_url) instead of in-band transfer. Clients that can accept larger payloads can follow the URL with an auth token.

SDK ergonomics:
Minimal callback surface (aim for < 100 LOC for client):
- onPartialText(text, seq) — invoked for every tok frame (clients can buffer or render incrementally)
- onToolFrame(frame) — invoked for tool_start/tool_arg/tool_commit; frame.id maps across calls
- onFinal(summary) — final frame with checksum and structured_url
- confirmTool(id, client_meta) — client calls to confirm tool execution; returns a promise/future resolved when tool_commit arrives
Other considerations:
- Provide a tiny JS reference library (40–80 lines) that wraps the newline-delimited frames and exposes the 3 callbacks + confirmTool. This should be published as hosted-sdk/microstream adapter.
- Native mobile SDKs (iOS/Android) should expose the same signatures; recommend using event streams that are cheap to integrate into mobile UI cycles.

Observability and telemetry requirements (what product needs):
- Track p50/p95 token-to-display latencies per region and per client type (native vs webview).
- Instrument counts of tool_start events per session and tool_commit success rate.
- Track resume attempts and resume success ratio (useful to tune baseline retention window of server-side token buffers).

Performance tradeoffs and server endpoints:
- Microstream increases number of packets/requests vs chunked streaming; will increase CPU scheduling overhead. We should limit microstream to shorter responses (suggest limit to <= 1024 tokens) or offer adaptive fallthrough where server switches to chunked frames after N tokens.
- Consider a "compact token encoding" (binary) as future opt-in to reduce bytes on the wire for extreme bandwidth cases.

Security and privacy notes:
- When structured_url is used, ensure signed short-lived pre-signed URLs (no PII leakage in URL path).
- Tool args should be sanitized server-side before emitting to clients. Document strong warnings for clients that auto-execute tool frames.

Compatibility matrix (rough):
- Web desktop: support microstream but default to chunked streaming.
- Mobile native: recommend microstream as default for poor networks; expose toggle in SDK to opt-in to chunked for final fidelity.
- Embedded / IoT: microstream default.

Open questions / tradeoffs to decide:
- Should tool_arg be allowed to include multi-chunk binary payloads (e.g., attachments)? If yes, we need an out-of-band upload flow.
- Should we provide a server-side option to auto-confirm small idempotent tools? (e.g., purely informational queries)
- Resume buffer window: 30s? 2 minutes? Need SRE guidance on memory/cost.
- Final checksum: which algorithm do we standardize on? sha256 is fine but heavier; maybe a shorter fingerprint for mobile.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Product: confirm priority and acceptance criteria with growth pilots (Maya) — due 2026-03-17
- Eng serving runtime: feasibility check for token-level replay buffer and sequencing guarantees (Arjun) — due 2026-03-24 (blocked on ENG-1248)
- SDK: spike a tiny JS adapter and a mobile pseudocode example (Samir) — spike ready 2026-03-21
- CS: identify 2 pilot customers to try microstream in low-bandwidth regions (Lina) — reach out by 2026-03-14

Notes to self / rough benchmarks to record when we get a spike:
- baseline token p50 with current chunking on iPhone 12 on 4G: ~210ms (measured, internal)
- target microstream p50: <100ms
- expected increase in server-side connections/frames: +20–40% depending on workload

Slack threads / refs: #hosted-api-streaming, #mobile-sdk-infra, PR 402 discusses typed schema header; see linked artifacts above.

Rough UX sketches (todo: upload pngs to confluence):
- Live caret streaming: render tokens as they arrive; show soft-confirm states for tool suggestions (dismissable card)
- Tool confirmation modal: shows tool name, arg preview, "execute" / "cancel" buttons; on execute, SDK calls confirmTool and shows spinner until tool_commit with outcome

End of sketch. This doc is intentionally terse and iterative. Expect follow-ups with protocol wire examples and a tiny JS reference implementation.
